title: Checks for undocumented public module definitions.
summary: Public modules should be documented via docstrings to outline their purpose and contents. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.70.

title: Checks for undocumented public class definitions.
summary: Public classes should be documented via docstrings to outline their purpose and behavior. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.70.

title: Checks for undocumented public method definitions.
summary: Public methods should be documented via docstrings to outline their purpose and behavior. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.70.

title: Checks for undocumented public function definitions.
summary: Public functions should be documented via docstrings to outline their purpose and behavior. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.70.

title: Checks for undocumented public package definitions.
summary: Public packages should be documented via docstrings to outline their purpose and contents. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.70.

title: Checks for undocumented magic method definitions.
summary: Magic methods (methods with names that start and end with double underscores) are used to implement operator overloading and other special behavior. Such methods should be documented via docstrings to outline their behavior. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.70.

title: Checks for undocumented public class definitions, for nested classes.
summary: Public classes should be documented via docstrings to outline their purpose and behavior. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.70.
message_templates: Missing docstring in public nested class

title: Checks for public __init__ method definitions that are missing docstrings.
summary: Public __init__ methods are used to initialize objects. __init__ methods should be documented via docstrings to describe the method's behavior, arguments, side effects, exceptions, and any other information that may be relevant to the user. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.70.
